title: First 100 Days Onboarding Playbook — Enterprise Customers
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a practical, modular playbook for enterprise customers covering the first 100 days after contract signature. It combines technical onboarding, adoption milestones, risk signals for renewal teams, and sample communications. It is intentionally lightweight — pick the sections that fit the customer tier (pilot vs. production) and the chosen deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private).

Intended audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) / Onboarding Engineers
- Account Execs (for renewal signal handoff)
- Support & SRE for operational runbooks

High-level objectives (first 100 days):
1) Prove core value: ensure customer can run a representative workload end-to-end with acceptable latency and cost.
2) Establish reliability baseline and alerting/SLAs for their environment.
3) Drive adoption of 1–3 product pathways (e.g., chat API for product feature, embeddings for search, Redwood Optimize suggestions).
4) Capture metrics and success stories to justify expansion/renewal.

Success metrics (example KPIs):
- Time-to-first-successful-call: <= 7 days from kickoff for hosted; <= 14 days for Dedicated/Private.
- Baseline 95th latency promise established and verified for representative prompt set.
- Active usage: >= 1k tokens/day or >= 300 embeddings/week depending on workload by day 60 (adjust per contract).
- Integration checkpoints passed (security signoff, data-flow, monitoring) by day 45.
- Customer health score >= 75 by day 100.

Kickoff checklist (pre-day-0 items):
- Contract & onboarding MSA signed (sales sign-off).
- Named technical contacts and SSO/KMS owners identified.
- Decide deployment mode + initial capacity: hosted vs. dedicated commit vs. private install.
- Route for billing and Admin Console access provisioned.
- Shared Confluence space / Slack channel created.
- Quick status call scheduled: 30–60 minutes 

0–14 days: baseline setup and early wins
Goals: enable initial access, validate API calls, and run a small smoke test.
Must-do items:
- Provision API key or dedicated endpoint and verify connectivity (SE).
- Run standard smoke prompt set (attached) to assert response shapes and latencies.
- Security review: collect IP allowlist, confirm KMS/HSM access if Private.
- Instrument telemetry: ensure request IDs, latency, errors surface in Console/Datadog.
- Sample deliverable: "First-call report" (CSM sends a short note with sample tokens, latency, top errors).
Communications: send 1st-week recap with screenshots and next steps.

15–45 days: integration and validation
Goals: integrate with product, run load/throughput tests, and establish monitoring.
Must-do items:
- Integration checklist: SDKs installed, environment variables, auth flows tested.
- Running a representative workload: SE to help create an automated test harness that runs the customer's top 10 prompts conversationally.
- Latency & cost baseline: collect token distribution, average response time, and estimated token cost per feature.
- Autoscaling & routing policy review (for Dedicated): set initial burst and scale thresholds.
- KV/prefix cache decisions: discuss caching strategy for high QPS patterns.
- Optional: Enable Redwood Optimize suggestions and agree on a trial quantization profile for evaluation.
Deliverables:
- Integration signoff checklist (checkboxes for SDKs, auth, telemetry)
- Runbook for common errors (401/403, model-incompatible requests, kv-cache misses)

46–100 days: adoption, optimization, and renewal signals
Goals: expand usage, run optimization experiments, and prepare renewal signals.
Must-do items:
- Adoption play: identify 1–3 internal champions and ship an internal launch (tracking support tickets, internal demos).
- Experiment: test one latency/cost tradeoff (e.g., smaller quantized variant + caching) and track quality delta on a prompt set.
- Quality monitoring: set up periodic evals against a gold prompt set. Flag regressions >5% BLEU/ROUGE or manually reviewed quality drop.
- Business outcomes: capture a short case snippet showing time saved or user engagement uplift.
- Renewal early-warning triggers (handbook):
  - Low usage: <40% expected units for two successive weeks by day 80.
  - Active defects: >3 sev2 incidents in 30 days.
  - Security backlog items unresolved by day 60.
  - Significant unaddressed quality regressions.
When a trigger fires: immediately notify AE + solutions lead and run a 7-day remediation sprint.

Customer health scoring (example inputs):
- Usage velocity (30% weight)
- Feature breadth (20% weight — proportion of targeted features adopted)
- Reliability (20% weight — incidents, latency SLOs)
- Engagement (15% weight — meetings, demos, champions)
- Satisfaction (15% weight — CSAT/NPS from pilot users)
Thresholds: >=80 green, 60–79 yellow (action plan required), <60 red (escalate).

Playbook snippets: sample email templates
- Kickoff invite (concise): 30–45 minute session — goals, roles, success metrics, required artifacts.
- 14-day checkpoint: short list of results, blockers, next 2 weeks' owners.
- 60-day adoption review: metrics snapshot, optimization experiments, ask for advocate intro.

Technical runbook highlights (for SE/SRE):
- Verify model variant compatibility: ensure requested architecture matches runtime kernels (note differences between quantized variants and full-precision models).
- Observability onboarding: confirm logs contain token counts, truncated prompts, memory pressure events.
- Scaling incident play: if 95p latency > target for 30 minutes — toggle fallback to cheaper variant + raise capacity request to infra.

Renewal-focused artifacts to capture by day 80:
- Executive one-pager with metrics (usage growth, reliability, cost per 1k tokens) and customer quotes.
- ROI snapshot: estimated cost savings or revenue enablement from using Redwood vs. self-hosted baseline.
- Risk register with mitigations and ownership.

Common playbook variations (pick one):
- "Pilot-first": shorter cadence, focus on product-market fit of an LLM feature. Goals: 0–30 day PoC, 31–60 grow to beta users.
- "Security-led enterprise": heavier emphasis on Private deployment, KMS validation, SOC2 artifacts; add extra 30 days for compliance signoffs.
- "Burst-scale": Dedicated capacity + autoscaling policies; include capacity burn-rate planning and cost-forecast board.

Templates (attached sections to copy into customer doc):
- 1-line success statement (for execs)
- 90/100-day milestone checklist with owners and dates
- Runbook command snippets (curl examples, example SDK call)
- Quality evaluation checklist for prompt sets

Risks and mitigations:
- Slow SSO/KMS approval: mitigation = provide temporary scoped API key and strict IP allowlist, add parallel security workshop.
- Unexpected latency under load: mitigation = ramp traffic gradually, enable prefix caching, schedule infra capacity increase.
- Quality regressions with quantized model: mitigation = rollback to verified model snapshot, run A/B evals, document thresholds for rollback.

Hand-off to renewals (by day 90–100):
- CSM to prepare a 1-page renewal brief for AE with: current health score, top wins, open risks, recommended renewal/expansion ask, required support level.
- Schedule a stakeholder review with exec summary and next-step ask.

Notes and open questions (working):
- Should we standardize "expected unit" definitions per vertical? (e.g., search vs. chat) — action: product ops to propose template.
- For Dedicated customers, define a standard "burst credit" policy in the contract to avoid ad-hoc capacity upgrades.

Attachments / links to templates (in linked_artifacts):
- CS-Onboarding-Runbooks (Confluence)
- Jira backlog for onboarding tasks (see keys above)
- Sample scripts repo for smoke tests

Quick references (cheat-sheet):
- Day 0–14: access + smoke test + telemetry on
- Day 15–45: integration + baseline + monitoring
- Day 46–100: optimize + adoption + renewal prep

If you're using this doc: please copy into the customer's Confluence folder and update the milestone dates. Mark this doc as the single source for the first-100-day artifacts and link any post-100-day plans separately.

Last updated notes:
- 2026-03-10: moved renewal triggers earlier to surface risk at day 60; added explicit 7-day remediation sprint process.
